note: PLUGIN-004 apply backpressure: a plugin can produce faster than the core reads, and src/plugin/streams.zig gives the two streams different behavior under pressure. Protocol frames are never dropped - a dropped frame desynchronizes the exchange, and a protocol that silently loses one is worse than one that stalls - so a full frame buffer returns a defined boundary and the producer waits, and consuming a frame is what lets it resume, which the test drives explicitly. Diagnostics are dropped oldest-first once their bounded buffer is full and the drop count is reported, because a log line is not worth stalling a build and the loss should be visible rather than implied. The test asserts the queued frames are exactly those produced, in order, with none lost. Fault proof: dropping the oldest protocol frame instead of applying backpressure makes the frame-sequence assertion fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
